title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Entry — Crestview Coffee Roasters, Inc.
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III entry IC memo recommending acquisition of Crestview Coffee Roasters, Inc. at $493M enterprise value (13.5x LTM Adj. EBITDA). Crestview is a vertically integrated DTC premium coffee brand with $270M LTM revenue and $36.5M LTM EBITDA. The investment thesis centers on subscription flywheel recurring revenue, DTC channel expansion (22% to 44% of mix), roasting capacity-driven margin expansion, and fragmented specialty coffee market consolidation. Base case projects a Year 5 exit at ~$1.01B EV yielding 2.7x MoIC and 22% gross IRR. Total sources/uses of $509M funded by $213M senior secured debt, $264M sponsor equity, and $32M management rollover. IC recommendation is unanimous: INVEST — PROCEED TO CLOSE.

key_quotes.quote: DTC subscription flywheel creates durable recurring revenue with exceptional unit economics. Subscription revenue is growing at 38% YoY and carries 71% gross margin vs. 52% for wholesale.

We believe this is one of the highest-quality consumer-DTC assets we have evaluated and that the entry valuation of 13.5x EBITDA is justified by the subscription unit economics, brand strength, and margin expansion opportunity.
Current DTC e-commerce (22% of revenue) is heavily underpenetrated vs. comparable DTC CPG brands that achieve 40–60% DTC mix at scale.

Crestview has the brand, supply chain depth, and operational infrastructure to consolidate 2–3 regional roasters during the hold period, expanding geographic presence and manufacturing capacity at attractive entry prices.

Negotiated 4-year employment agreement with 18-month gardening clause and $8M retention package; COO Elena Ruiz (ex-Blue Apron COO) is capable successor in near term; Korn Ferry completed senior leadership bench assessment with favorable findings.

growth_drivers: DTC subscription flywheel with 84% 12-month retention and 6.8x LTV/CAC
Expansion of DTC/e-commerce channel from 22% to 44% of revenue
Roasting capacity additions reducing third-party tolling costs and improving margins
Stable wholesale and B2B cash flow funding DTC investment
Fragmented specialty coffee market consolidation of 2–3 regional roasters
risks: Coffee commodity price volatility (green coffee beans)
DTC customer acquisition cost inflation (paid social, search)
Subscription churn acceleration in economic downturn
Key-man dependency on Founder/CEO Tom Crestview
Food safety and supply chain disruption risk
